style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: A semiconductor component warehouse aisle at late afternoon, 200mm telephoto compression, stacked pallet racks of sealed black memory-chip trays stretching into flat compressed distance. Hard low raking sunlight from the left through high clerestory windows, casting deep diagonal shadows across a concrete floor. Palette graphite, safety yellow, bone white. Materials brushed aluminum rack rails, black anti-static polymer trays, weathered concrete. Asymmetric composition with the first rack off-centre and rows receding to the right, no people, no text, no logos. Deep industrial contrast, crystal-clear air, 16:9.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, illegible labels
rationale: The story is about the scale of inventory and purchase commitments colliding with quarterly price increases; telephoto compression makes the accumulated stock and future obligations feel physical and immense, not like a product still life.
cue: Your Stock Is the Cheaper Memory: 5% vs 20%
subject: rows of sealed memory stock trays on pallet racks stretching into compressed distance
core_thesis: When a purchased input reprices faster each quarter than stock costs to hold, the buffer becomes a priced hedge and the decision shifts from safety stock to committed days of supply.
core_conflict: quarterly component price acceleration versus the 5-7.5% quarterly cost of holding stock
composition: asymmetric long-lens compression with the first rack off-centre and rows receding to the right
